user.title: Stage Utility
user.description: Point Home Assistant at your Stage Utility server and give it a cue token. Mint one in Stage Utility under Settings, Automation, Calling cues.

data_description.host: An address on your network: 192.168.1.50, 192.168.1.50:8788, or http://stage-utility:8788. Plain HTTP on port 8788 is assumed when you leave those off.
data_description.token: The secret shown once when the token was minted, starting su_.

error.cannot_connect: That address did not answer. Check the server is running and reachable on this network.
error.too_old: That Stage Utility is running, but it is older than 1.18.0 and has no cue manifest. Update it, or point this at a server on the beta channel.
error.invalid_auth: Stage Utility refused that token. Mint a new one and try again.
error.invalid_host: That is not an address this integration can use.

abort.already_configured: This Stage Utility server is already set up.

init.title: Stage Utility
init.description: How this server appears in Home Assistant.

data.reload_homekit_bridge: Reload the HomeKit Bridge when cues change

data_description.show_in_sidebar: Adds an entry that opens the server's own web interface inside Home Assistant. A Home Assistant served over HTTPS cannot frame a plain-HTTP server, so the entry is left out and the log says so.
data_description.reload_homekit_bridge: A HomeKit Bridge only works out which entities to publish when it reloads, so a cue added or deleted in Stage Utility leaves the Apple Home app a switch short, or showing a deleted one as No Response. With this on, every bridge that could be publishing these cues is reloaded fifteen seconds after the cue list stops changing. Turn it off and reload the bridge by hand instead, under Settings, Devices & services, HomeKit Bridge, Reload.
